Problem 2:

Write a function that uses a for loop that, for each iteration, randomly draws 5 observations from an exponential distribution with “rate” parameter 1 (use rexp()) and calculates its “mean”. It should do this 10,000 times. Choose an appropriate plot to plot the distribution of “means”.

  • Solution: We want to fill a vector with values. We should create this vector beforehand using the vector() function.

  • We want to create a vector of size 10 and we want its values to be numeric.

  • Then we want to randomly draw 5 observations from an exponential distribution with “rate” parameter 1 (use rexp(5, rate = 1)) and calculates its “mean”

  • Now we want to create a vector that has length of 10 and its values are mean of this randomly selected exponential functions

  • Now we want to draw the histogram. But we need to have a data frame. Let us define a data frame.

  • Now we can draw a histogram

    • Now, let’s solve the problem all in one step
#Create vector size of 10000
B <- 10000
means_for <- vector("double", B)

#Loop 10000 times
for (i in seq_len(B)) {
  means_for[[i]] <- mean(rexp(5, rate=1))
}

#Create data frame and histogram
df_for <- tibble(sample_mean = means_for)
ggplot(df_for, aes(x=sample_mean)) +
  geom_histogram(bins=30, fill = 'blue', color='black') +
  labs(
    title="Distribution of Sample Means with For Loop",
    x="Sample Mean",
    y="Frequency"
  )

2_a:

  • Repeat part 1 by using a map_*() function.
#Calculate sample mean from each iteration in the rexp(rate=1)
means_map <- map_dbl(1:10000, \(i) mean(rexp(5, rate=1)))

#convert vector into data frame
df_map <- tibble(sample_mean = means_map)

#create histogram
ggplot(df_map, aes(x = sample_mean)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "blue", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Sample Means",
    x = "Sample Mean",
    y = "Frequency"
  )

2_b:

  • Repeat part 1 by using the replicate() function.
#Repeat randomization and mean calculation 10000 times
means_rep <- replicate(10000, mean(rexp(5, rate=1)))

#Store results in tibble
df_rep <- tibble(sample_mean = means_rep)

#Plot distribution
ggplot(df_rep, aes(x = sample_mean)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "blue", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Sample Means (replicate, n = 5)",
    x = "Sample Mean",
    y = "Frequency"
  )

2_c:

  • Use a another for loop that will print out plots for sample sizes of 5, 10, and 20 observations (instead of just 5).
# Define vector of sample sizes
sample_sizes <- c(5, 10, 20)

#For loop iterates through each sample
for (n in sample_sizes) {
  means <- vector("double", 10000)
  for (i in 1:10000) {
    means[[i]] <- mean(rexp(n, rate=1))
  }
  df_n <- tibble(sample_mean = means)
  p <- ggplot(df_n, aes(x = sample_mean)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "blue", color = "black") +
    labs(
      title = paste("Distribution of Sample Means (n =", n, ")"),
      x = "Sample Mean",
      y = "Frequency"
    )
  
  print(p)
}

Problem 3:

  • Use and show R coding to calculate the “standard deviation” for each variable of the data table mtcars using the “Special For Loop Method”.

Note:

  • There are two methods. Please see a quick explanation for both methods in below:

    • Method 1:
  multi_return <- function() {
    my_list <- list("color" = "red", "size" = 20, "shape" = "round")
    return(my_list) 
  }
a <- multi_return()
a$color
[1] "red"
a<- multi_return()
a$shape
[1] "round"
a<- multi_return()
a$size
[1] 20
  • Method 2. The “Special For Loop Method”
output <- vector("double", ncol(df))  # 1. output (use appropriate data frame instead of df)
for (i in seq_along(df)) {            # 2. sequence
  output[[i]] <- median(df[[i]])      # 3. body
}
output
  • Solution: coding to calculate the “standard deviation” for each variable
# Get output vector with correct length and type
output <- vector("double", ncol(mtcars))
names(output) <- colnames(mtcars)

#Sequence mtcars columns
for(i in seq_along(mtcars)) {
  output[[i]] <- sd(mtcars[[i]])
}

Problem 4:

Generate a sequence of dates from January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2025, spaced by every two months. Extract the year, quarter, and ISO week number for each date.

#generate data sequence  from selected dates with two month spaces
dates_seq <- seq(from = ymd("2015-01-01"), to = ymd('2025-12-31'), by= "2 months")

#Extract year, quarter, and ISO week number into tibble
dates_tbl <- tibble(
  date     = dates_seq,
  year     = year(dates_seq),
  quarter  = quarter(dates_seq),
  iso_week = isoweek(dates_seq)
)

Problem 5

Given the following dates, compute the difference in months and weeks between each consecutive pair.

sample_dates <- c("2018-03-15", "2020-07-20", "2023-01-10", "2025-09-05")
#input sample dates
sample_dates <- c("2018-03-15", "2020-07-20", "2023-01-10", "2025-09-05")

#turn string dates into objects
dates_parse <- ymd(sample_dates)

#define start dates and end dates
start_dates <- dates_parse[-length(dates_parse)]
end_dates <- dates_parse[-1]

#calculate difference in months and dates between pairs
date_diffs <- tibble(
  pair        = paste(start_dates, "to", end_dates),
  diff_months = (start_dates %--% end_dates) / months(1),
  diff_weeks  = (start_dates %--% end_dates) / weeks(1)
)

date_diffs
# A tibble: 3 × 3
  pair                     diff_months diff_weeks
  <chr>                          <dbl>      <dbl>
1 2018-03-15 to 2020-07-20        28.2       123.
2 2020-07-20 to 2023-01-10        29.7       129.
3 2023-01-10 to 2025-09-05        31.8       138.

Problem 6

Given a list of mixed date formats, use map() and possibly() from purrr to safely convert them to Date format and extract the month name.

date_strings <- list("2023-06-10", "2022/12/25", "15-Aug-2021", "InvalidDate")
# Input list of date formats
date_strings <- list("2023-06-10", "2022/12/25", "15-Aug-2021", "InvalidDate")

#Wrap function in possibly() to handle errors
safe_parse <- possibly(
  function(x){
    as.Date(parse_date_time(x, orders = c("ymd", "dmy", "Ymd")))
  },
  otherwise = NA
)

#Apply safe parsing across all elements
parsed_dates <- map(date_strings, safe_parse)
Warning: All formats failed to parse. No formats found.
#wrap month in possibly() to handle errors
safe_month <- possibly(
  function(d) {
    if (is.na(d)) return(NA_character_)
    as.character(month(d, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE))
  },
  otherwise = NA_character_
)

#Apply safe month extraction across parsed dates
month_names <- map(parsed_dates, safe_month)

#Combine results
tibble(
  input      = unlist(date_strings),
  parsed     = do.call(c, parsed_dates),
  month_name = unlist(month_names)
)
# A tibble: 4 × 3
  input       parsed     month_name
  <chr>       <date>     <chr>     
1 2023-06-10  2023-06-10 June      
2 2022/12/25  2022-12-25 December  
3 15-Aug-2021 2021-08-15 August    
4 InvalidDate NA         <NA>
